rules.label: Income-based assistance: 0-250% FPL
rules.quote: Patients approved for Financial Assistance with an annual Family Income of 250% of FPL guidelines or less will receive a 100% discount on gross charges for care covered by this policy

rules.label: Income-based assistance: 251-400% FPL
rules.quote: Patients approved for Financial Assistance with an annual Family Income between 251% and 400% of FPL guidelines will receive a discount on gross charges as outlined in Appendix A

rules.label: Catastrophic Balance Financial Assistance
rules.quote: The Patient's outstanding single account balance due after all insurance or third-party payments and/or discounts (including the application of Financial Assistance based on family income alone) is greater than 50% of the Patient's total annual Family Income and Financial Resources combined

rules.label: Presumptive Eligibility
rules.quote: Patients granted Presumptive Eligibility for Financial Assistance will receive a 100% discount on gross charges for care covered by this policy

application.quote: 365 days from the date of the first post-discharge Billing Statement
30 days after notice of the initiation of one or more Extraordinary Collection Actions (ECA) has been provided

eca_not_before.quote: UCHealth will refrain from initiating ECAs for at least 365 days from the date the Hospital mails the first post-discharge Billing Statement

notes: Residency requirement (Colorado resident) applies to Financial Assistance but may be waived at hospital's sole discretion for unscheduled emergency services (B.2). UCHealth employees residing outside Colorado are exempt from residency requirement (A.9).

Services not covered: non-emergent/non-medically-necessary care (elective/cosmetic), transplant procedures, self-pay packages, single case agreements, grants & research, or when third party has legal obligation to pay (C.2).

Discounts for 251-400% FPL and Catastrophic assistance are facility-specific per Appendix A tables (AGB percentages). AGB discount applies; if self-pay discount > AGB, self-pay discount used instead (H.5, H.6).
Patients approved for Financial Assistance will not be charged more than Amount Generally Billed (AGB) for insured patients (H.5).
Presumptive eligibility only applies to current services and past accounts, not future services (G.4).
Application processing within 14 days of receipt (F.5). Income-based eligibility valid 365 days (≤250% FPL) or 180 days (251-400% FPL) from last signed application (F.6, F.7).
Incomplete applications denied but no ECAs initiated; 30-day notice with missing info provided; applicant can complete within application period or 30 days of notice (F.8).
ECAs reversed and refunds issued for overpayments >$1 upon approval (F.9).
No credit reporting or property liens for patient debt (I.7).
Four monthly billing statements sent before collections referral; insured accounts referred after 120 days unpaid, uninsured after 182 days (I.5).
Family definition: 2+ people related by birth/marriage/adoption residing together; members not responsible for patients 18+ (Definitions).
Financial Resources: cash, bank deposits, easily withdrawable assets (checking, savings, trusts, CDs) (Definitions).

Income includes wages, unemployment, workers comp, SSI, public assistance, veterans payments, survivor benefits, pension, interest, dividends, rents, royalties, estates, trusts, educational assistance, alimony, child support, outside assistance; excludes non-cash benefits (Definitions).
Provider coverage list maintained separately and updated quarterly (C.1).

findings.title: Covers everyone Colorado's Hospital Discounted Care protects

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: Patients and their households are eligible for Hospital Discounted Care if, during the required screening and application processes, they are determined to: Have a total household income at or below 250% of the Federal Poverty Guidelines (FPG), and Be residents of the State of Colorado.
IF REQUESTED BY THE PATIENT, A HEALTH-CARE FACILITY SHALL SCREEN AN INSURED PATIENT FOR DISCOUNTED CARE

findings.summary: Inconclusive: 1 of the model's rules were dropped by the quote and meaning checks, so a missing rule may be our error. Z3's case: A household of 3 earning $27,000 a year (98.8% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, insured, and not under-insured as the policy defines it, owing $10,000 meets every requirement, but no rule of this policy grants them help. Colorado law makes them eligible for Hospital Discounted Care.

findings.title: Ignores assets for Colorado-protected households

law.quote: THE METHODOLOGY MUST NOT CONSIDER A PATIENT'S ASSETS.

findings.summary: Proved: for households Colorado's law protects, savings and assets never changes the outcome.

findings.title: Doesn't require a Medicaid application first

law.quote: DENY DISCOUNTED CARE ON THE BASIS THAT THE PATIENT HAS NOT APPLIED FOR ANY PUBLIC BENEFITS PROGRAM

findings.summary: Proved: for households Colorado's law protects, whether they applied for Medicaid or other public programs never changes the outcome.

findings.title: No collection lawsuits or garnishment before day 182

law.quote: NO MEDICAL CREDITOR COLLECTING ON A DEBT FOR HOSPITAL SERVICES SHALL ENGAGE IN ANY PERMISSIBLE EXTRAORDINARY COLLECTION ACTIONS UNTIL ONE HUNDRED EIGHTY-TWO DAYS AFTER THE DATE THE PATIENT RECEIVES HOSPITAL SERVICES.

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: begin sending bills beginning 46 days after the patient's date of service or date of discharge

findings.summary: Proved: whatever day the first bill goes out, the policy's own timeline never allows a collection action before day 182 after care.
findings.domain: every first-bill day from day 46 to day 400

findings.title: Accepts applications for at least 181 days after care

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: Patients may complete a screening at any time within at least 181 days after their date of service or discharge, whichever is later

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: begin sending bills beginning 46 days after the patient's date of service or date of discharge

findings.summary: Proved: whatever day the first bill goes out (Colorado allows bills from day 46), the application window never closes before day 181 after care.
findings.domain: every first-bill day from day 46 to day 400

findings.title: Insured patients get 45 days after their first post-insurance bill

law.source: HCPF Hospital Discounted Care Operations Manual, Mar 31 2026
law.quote: At least 45 days from the date of the first bill after the patient's insurance adjustment, even if that date falls outside the normal 181-day window.

findings.summary: Proved: the window always stays open at least 45 days past the first bill.
findings.domain: every first-bill day from day 0 to day 400

findings.title: Payment plans capped at 4% of monthly income, done after 36 payments

law.quote: THE PATIENT IS NOT PAYING MORE THAN FOUR PERCENT OF THE PATIENT'S MONTHLY HOUSEHOLD INCOME ON A BILL FROM A HEALTH-CARE FACILITY
AFTER A CUMULATIVE THIRTY-SIX MONTHS OF PAYMENTS, CONSIDER THE PATIENT'S BILL PAID IN FULL

findings.summary: The policy states no payment-plan terms to check. Colorado's 4% / 36-month limits apply anyway.

findings.title: Application window of 240 days after the first bill (501(r))

law.quote: ends on the later of the 240th day after the date that the first post-discharge billing statement for the care is provided

findings.summary: Proved: for any first-bill day, applications stay open at least 240 days after it.
findings.domain: every first-bill day from day 0 to day 400

findings.title: No collection actions in the first 120 days after the first bill (501(r))

law.quote: for at least 120 days from the date the hospital facility provides the first post-discharge billing statement for the care

findings.summary: Proved: collection actions never start sooner than 120 days after the first bill.
findings.domain: every first-bill day from day 0 to day 400

findings.title: Earning less never means getting less help
findings.summary: Inconclusive: 1 of the model's rules were dropped by the quote and meaning checks, so a missing rule may be our error. Z3's case: A household of 3 earning $68,573 a year (251.0% of the poverty line), living in Colorado, uninsured, owing $10,000 gets no help; the same household earning more, at 251.36% of the poverty line, gets help (amount not stated). The written income bands leave a gap between them.
